newsitem.title: UK: SIB metal task force to issue paper soon.
newsitem.headline: SIB metal task force to issue paper soon.

text.p: A task force established by the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) to educate some metal market users is to issue a consultative document soon, Jane Lowe, head of Derivatives Market Supervision at the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said.
The SIB set up its committee of trade associations to address concerns over the risks and benefits involved with some London Metal Exchange (LME) practices.

"The task force has met twice now and is currently in the process of drafting guidance. This document will shortly be subject to industry consultation," Lowe said at the Financial Times World Aluminium Conference.

The SIB was asked by the LME to carry out a review of the exchange last June, following the announcement by Japan's Sumitomo Corp of losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading. The SIB made its report last December.
Lowe said some American respondents to the SIB review wanted an end to LME practices such as non-cash clearing, non-segration of accounts, and historic price carries.

"We concluded instead that it was important that market users understood the risks they were taking and were in a position to assess the trade-off between the risks and benefits of these practices," she added.
But the SIB decided to work with other regulators and the industry to ensure market-users were as well informed as possible.
The task force includes the International Wrought Copper Council, (IWCC), the International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI), the Futures and Options Association and SIB.
